reviews.text: A lovely little game! I love the charming pixel graphics (Pierre has a great style) and the gameplay is fun. I would have appreciated volume sliders instead of toggles, and the game going through the intro/logo screen each time you win a run is a bit obnoxious when you're doing several runs in a row. Otherwise, no complaints.

[h1][Neutral / Mixed Feelings] A bite of (overly) simple, middling arcade fun. (6.5/10) [/h1] I am glad there is a new indie game inspired by Puzzle Bobble. At 2 USD base price (and following regional pricing, seemingly; [i]thank you, dev[/i]), this is easy enough to almost recommend. But I’ll be honest, [i]if it was at 5USD, the simplicity of it would make me give a definite thumbs down[/i]. And [b]I don’t see myself replaying[/b] this game much, if ever. So, what’s the issue? I think there’s just a [b]lack of proper thought in its level design[/b]. On the starting difficulties, the game does feel like a breeze. But on “Hard” where you get more restrictive HP & orb count (your ammo to shoot), it becomes reasonably challenging enough that you’d need to play optimally. On paper. [h3](-) In practice however, the level design doesn’t really allow for much in the way of “optimal” play.[/h3] [b]These kinds of games can make you feel smart[/b] and give the rush of dopamine just right when you manage to [b]land a shot via side-wall bounces, or when you connect two clusters of the same color with 1 shot[/b]; therefore saving you +1 orb count. These opportunities do exist, thankfully. [b]But way too often[/b], I see levels that are very disjointed between the same-colored clusters; where the [b]gaps are 2 orbs distance or more[/b] and you really [b]can’t do much other than simply aiming[/b] at each cluster with the cognitive level of a 10 year old. Certain levels also really love to have “Wall spikes” on [i]both[/i] the left and right sides, nullifying any attempts at wall-bouncing since your orbs disappear upon touching them. I feel like if the spikes were more intermittent and there were gaps of normal bouncy walls; or if these spikes simply cause you to take HP damage but the orbs persist in behaving; it could be nice. Back on optimal connection-play; if there were more levels that utilized the principle of making same colors / color-changing orbs all be distanced by 1 orb-gap a lot more often, this game would be so much better, and the orb count limitation would be justified. [b](-) The item “Multi-orb” (color-changing shot), in theory, could fix this[/b] and allow you to connect different colored clusters; [b]if it works how I thought it would. Except it doesn’t[/b] work like a pure wild card. [b]It will always choose 1 color to change into, even [i]when it touches two[/i][/b] simultaneously. Why? [h3]It generally feels like some of the items could use more work, the base mechanic systems could be re-considered, and level elements could’ve had new objects to spice it up.[/h3] [h3]Information:[/h3] [b](•)Playtime: ~6 hours[/b] for 100% all achievements. Some of the Hard difficulties and wizards do feel like banging my head against the wall though. Especially Teleportation. But at least on Easy difficulty that wizard is the least mind-numbing compared to the rest, since having a fixed starting position often does force you to think. [b](•)Achievement felt otherwise reasonably obtainable.[/b] The icons are nice too. [h3](+) Pros:[/h3] [b](+) Good, chiptune-ish music.[/b] The one saving grace of the game I suppose, I do wish the soundtrack will be up on Youtube soon and I might buy it on steam once it’s out. Each wizard is a different take on the main motif, which I really loved going through one at a time. [b](+) Decently charming art.[/b] I enjoy the boss previews and the wizard designs. [h3](-) Cons:[/h3] [b](-) Simple, questionable base mechanics.[/b] At first glance it’s all fine, but the more I think about some things the more I wished they were changed. The main behavior of ‘slide along the bottom of the level’, while fun, could make the game be too easy for most wizards. The distance could be reduced by like 2 orb spots or something and have an item allow us a bigger range of slide. Econ (gold) also matters a bit in this game, and I wished there were more in the way of bonuses. What if the bonus gold ramps up on having lots of remainder orbs instead of a flat +1? Or if fully clearing a board with the help of bombs / multi orbs (even the normally indestructible obstacles) would give some extra gold? It doesn’t, so rip buying bombs. You also have no ways of rerolling the shop. [b](-) Pointless items?[/b] There’s a few econ items here which I find myself caring about, like the Voucher or Nuggets. But some felt worse. All the 5 elemental runes are interchangeable and meh; because it only gives an extra “+1 gold” on clearing clusters of 5 orbs or more of a particular color. But the issue is bigger clusters don’t even do much. “5” is the minimum, but destroying “5” vs “10” still gives +1 in both cases. [b]Worth pointing out that it’s not easy to even make clusters of 5+ if we, the player, don’t have the ability to change our current shot into a stacking, non-destroying version to slowly build up clusters[/b]; normally shooting a 2 into a 3 just destroys it. And while there’s an item that allows you to preview your next orb, there’s none that allows you to swap between two afaik. There’s also the fact that [b]wasting your shots on trying to make a bigger cluster[/b] (turning a 3 to 5 by shooting 1 orb near it; hoping to connect it with another) also [b]means you lose out on the +1 orb count excess[/b] that would normally [b]give you gold anyways[/b] once you clear the level. Even when you have runes, it feels like [b]the incentive is still to just play normally[/b] instead of around maximizing its value. [b]Gold Nugget item[/b], which is slightly more expensive, just gives a flat +3 per level iirc without relying on level design RNG on what colors you get. It just makes the runes feel like an uninteresting noob trap in comparison. [b](-) Lacking level objects.[/b] Enough said. There’s wall spikes. Among the generated, on-level static stuff, there are spiky orbs that do the same thing in destroying your shots and you have to play around them. Then there’s stone orbs, basic indestructible simple walls, and mirror/echo ones that change into what you touch it with. And poison which you can shoot and get in your orb pool, but do more damage if you leave too much. That’s it? [b]What if we had some sort of portal orbs[/b] that allow our shots to teleport between one point to the next while keeping the trajectory? Some sort of [b]mirrors, or bouncy pegs[/b] in the middle of level so that there would be more bounce opportunities and smart shots without relying on the outer level’s wall/edges? I feel like things like this would give so much life to the level design if they existed. But judging from the current designs, I doubt they would even be implemented in a good way. [b](-) The wizards also don’t feel distinct or interesting.[/b] For me, the only wizards that I’ll somewhat care to play after 100%ing are the base (with Scope / trajectory preview), the Bomber, the Teleportation (fixed random starting points, no more sliding across the bottom which also arguably makes it too easy and you don’t need to rely on bounces), and maybe Invocation [clear big clusters at once = get more orbs]. The others feel like simple gimmicks that I don’t care much for. The one that starts with gold nugget vs runes just give a slight twist on econ but feel interchangeable, and Pay-with-HP isn’t much different. [h1]In the end, I admit it’s cheap enough to get anyway if you just want some short, mindless fun, but do at your own risk![/h1]

I loved Pierre's previous game, "Tiny Folks". It was simple, but required strategy and resource management. Though I love the Puzzle Bobble games, this game was just too easy. It's pretty much predetermined where you're supposed to shoot, as apposed to on-the-spot thinking with randomness. The graphics, as always, are great, I just didn't enjoy the game. I won't refund it though, cuz I know Pierre can make good stuff :3
Classic gameplay, though lacking polish. Fine given the approach, but the old arcade games still feel better

Technically I have over 17 hours on Orb Tower but Steam wouldn't count it since I was offline on a road trip while playing it. Orb Tower was so good I sat in a car for 17 hours playing Orb Tower instead of going on my phone at any point. Holy peak. This was such a wonderful game and one of my favorites. My boyfriend and I fight over who gets to play it since we share a steam library. I finished the entire game, played it a few different times. I have all the achievements and I love playing with new strategies and builds. I would love an update to Orb Tower please please please please please

Great casual / arcade game when you want to play something for a few minutes or just want to kill some time without committing to anything. Runs clean and the sound effects are nice. The pixel art is honestly charming and doesn't detract from the experience at all. If you grew up on the old Pop Cap games and 2000s favorites like Dynomite!, you'll enjoy this, too.

My girlfriend and I really really love this game. It is the only game I come back to over and over and over again. I played the free trial somewhere for hours before seeing how affordable it is and I bought it and it is SO worth it, I've beat the game now but it's still something I play whenever I have some down time, trying to do a run with no damage or collecting gold. When my girlfriend gets an unlucky orb we say "Pierre hates me" and it's joined our daily lexicon. Pierre is our genius and this game is the best game of all time please buy it please we love Pierre we love Orb Tower
